manager_rule: When building the Kelvin stub candidate set for each round, the stub compiler MUST emit directed stubs for /SENSEC{N}_HI and /SENSEC{N}_LO whenever AT LEAST ONE of those two nets for cable N has unconnected ratlines in the immediately preceding round's failing_reasons or per-net unconnected metrics — it MUST NOT require both nets to be failing (AND condition) before including cable N in the stub set. After each round where kelvin_unrouted > 0 or failing_reasons contains any /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO entry, the manager MUST audit the stub compiler's triggering predicate to confirm it uses an OR condition; if any cable N has a partial Kelvin failure (exactly one of /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO in failing_reasons while the other is absent) and the compiler emitted zero stubs for that cable, log 'kelvin_partial_failure_compiler_gap' with fields: (a) round number, (b) cable index N, (c) which net is failing and which is not, and (d) whether stubs were present for that cable in the compiler's raw output. Treat the absence of stubs for a partially-failing cable as a compiler_kelvin_skip event under Rule 18 for the missing net, halt FR dispatch, and require before resumption: (1) a code fix demonstrating OR-based triggering, (2) a test showing that a synthetic board state with only /SENSEC{N}_HI unconnected (and /SENSEC{N}_LO fully routed) produces a stub entry for /SENSEC{N}_HI in the compiler raw output, and (3) explicit written authorization. This rule is additive to Rules 18 and 19: those rules detect that a Kelvin stub is absent after the fact; this rule targets the compiler's input predicate as a distinct, earlier failure mode.
